A film by Dr. Natalie Petouhoff

What settles a nun in meditation
and a man in a
maximum-security cell?

We went looking — from the Dalai Lama's monasteries in Dharamshala to a chaplaincy at Rikers Island — and found the same answer in both rooms.

EMPATHY: THE PURSUIT OF JOY · A feature documentary + series · Therapeutic entertainment

The problem

The wise choice doesn't lose on merit.
It loses at the moment of need.

Stress, loneliness, numbness — and always within reach, a perfectly engineered fix: the scroll, the drink, the cart. Instant. Personalized. Frictionless.

These aren't bad habits. They're the most sophisticated behavioral technology ever built — engineered for nervous systems that are already cornered. Contemplative practice wins the same moment, and has for three thousand years. It builds what the quick fixes only counterfeit: agency, meaning, connection. It just never got a delivery system.

The reframe

Public translation.

The barrier isn't belief — it's translation. People don't reject this wisdom; they never receive it in a form their skepticism, their nervous system, or their worst moment can accept.

This project builds the translation layer between 3,000-year-old wisdom and a skeptical, pluralistic, overwhelmed modern audience — empathy as the method, science as the passport. Not a film about meditation. The delivery system the medicine never had.

Why now

The ancients had the insight.
What's new is the instrument.

  • Measurable regulation — before/after neuroscience on real audiences: watch it happen in your own body and brain
  • Personalized feedback — the adoption lever the wellness industry never had
  • Format science — testing what the nervous system will actually accept: story, sound, rhythm, synchrony, breath

This film could not have been made twenty years ago. The wisdom is ancient; the proof is brand new.

The work

A 90-minute feature and a series.
A new category: therapeutic entertainment.

Real people — monks and maximum-security prisoners, doctors, artists, mothers, fathers — facing life's beautiful, brutal, in-between.

Every piece is both medicine and instrument: documentary segments, original score, breath-paced and binaural sound, contemplative visual art — built, measured, revised, tested. We don't make media and hope. We run a measured intervention with a film as its instrument.

The proof engine

What survives a skeptical room.

  • Measured interventions — before/after outcomes on self- and co-regulation, empathy, meaning, flourishing
  • A peer-reviewed paper — rare in this category; it converts a film into evidence
  • Case studies — science-backed material that raises funding and validation for the whole field
  • Co-regulation focus — loneliness is the wound; a room full of nervous systems settling together is the one thing the scroll can never offer
Distribution before production

The audience is already in the room.

A worldwide network — researchers, well-being organizations, practitioners, educators, artists, community leaders — is screening prototypes and shaping the work right now. They are our collaborators. When the film is ready, they are our distributors.

The question every producer fears — "will anyone watch?" — was answered before a frame was shot. Event-based community screenings, curricula, and measured impact outlive the release window.

The ask

Three tiers. Each complete on its own.

  • PROOF — $250–400k · finish the feature edit, complete the measurement round, festival + impact-screening run
  • TRANSLATION — $750k–1.2M · + scientifically-composed soundtrack, vertical content engine, series pilot package
  • CATEGORY — $2–3M · + series order package, immersive experience build, global screening + curriculum program

Four lanes open: grants (Templeton submitted) · equity · brand sponsorship · community funding. Final budget detail available under NDA.
